subject.title: message tool: Feishu send action polluted by poll schema/guard prevents file send

question: Should plain `message(action="send")` treat any content-bearing poll fields as an error, or should OpenClaw hide/strip poll creation fields so ordinary sends cannot be blocked by accidental schema fill?
rationale: Current main intentionally allows metadata-only padding but still rejects content-bearing poll fields on `send`; changing that boundary affects the model-facing tool contract across channels, not only Feishu.

options.title: Action-scope poll fields
options.body: Expose poll creation fields only for poll actions or channel-specific poll tools, reducing accidental model fill while preserving strict poll validation.

options.title: Strip poll fields on send
options.body: Treat `action="send"` as authoritative and drop poll creation fields before delivery, improving send reliability but hiding contradictory caller intent.

options.title: Keep strict content guard
options.body: Continue rejecting content-bearing poll fields on `send` and require stronger live evidence before changing the shared contract.

recommendation.title: Action-scope poll fields
recommendation.body: Expose poll creation fields only for poll actions or channel-specific poll tools, reducing accidental model fill while preserving strict poll validation.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged poll gating and schema consistency history is the strongest current signal for the shared send/poll boundary.
